title: Audit log retention enforcement worker (batch deletes/TTL, safety limits, idempotency, metrics)
creator: Ethan Park
project: Enterprise Security & Compliance Foundation: Retention controls + compliance reporting pack
related_prs: GitHub (redwood): PR #18491 - Add retention enforcement worker for audit logs with batching, rate limits, metrics, and safe retries
GitHub (observability-pack): PR #207 - Dashboards/alerts for retention enforcement jobs
summary: Implement the v1 retention enforcement worker for the audit log datastore. The worker must enforce per-tenant effective retention policies with guardrails and legal hold/exception semantics, while remaining safe (rate-limited), idempotent, and observable. This is the enforcement leg of the Retention Controls initiative and will be used as core evidence for enterprise security reviews (provable deletion behavior + auditability).
background: We already have (or are implementing in parallel) the retention policy schema + validation (ENG-2911) and effective policy evaluation (ENG-2912). This ticket adds the actual enforcement loop for audit logs: apply retention cutoffs to the audit log storage backend, respecting legal holds and exceptions, and producing metrics/audit artifacts showing when enforcement ran and what it deleted. The ADR calls for a hybrid approach: storage TTL/partition TTL where available, otherwise scheduled deletion workers with explicit safety limits and monitoring.
scope_in: Audit log retention enforcement for Hosted/Dedicated control plane audit log storage. Enforcement is scheduled and can be triggered manually by on-call with guardrails. Must respect legal holds and exception flags. Must emit structured audit events/records about enforcement runs (who/what/when), and expose metrics for lag, throughput, and errors.
scope_out: Not enforcing retention across every operational log stream (infra logs governed by SRE/vendor constraints). Not implementing customer-configurable retention for raw inference payload content in v1. Not implementing arbitrary per-event deletion outside the retention cutoff (e.g., "right to be forgotten" workflows) beyond existing privacy processes.
proposed_approach: Create a dedicated worker ("retention-enforcer") that runs on a schedule (hourly by default, configurable) and iterates per tenant + per region over eligible audit log partitions. For each tenant, compute cutoff timestamp from the effective policy (policy engine) and apply deletion for events older than cutoff. Deletions happen in bounded batches (e.g., 5k-25k rows per batch) with a global runtime limit, per-tenant rate limit, and DB load protections. Use an idempotent delete predicate (created_at < cutoff AND tenant_id = X AND legal_hold = false AND exception_hold = false) so retries are safe. Record each run in a small "retention_enforcement_runs" table and emit job-level logs with a stable run_id for correlation. Support a dry-run mode that reports what would be deleted without mutating data.
datastore_notes: Audit logs are stored in a partitioned table (daily partitions) with tenant_id indexed. Where partition TTL is feasible, we still keep the worker as the authoritative enforcement path in v1 to support per-tenant variation and legal hold semantics. Worker should prefer partition drop/truncate only when it is safe with respect to tenant scoping and holds; otherwise use row deletes. If the underlying store supports TTL expressions per partition that can incorporate tenant/hold predicates, we can phase to more TTL-based enforcement later (tracked separately).
safety_limits: Hard safety constraints: (1) per-run max rows deleted (default 250k), (2) per-tenant max rows deleted (default 50k), (3) max runtime (default 15 minutes), (4) DB query timeout (e.g., 5-10 seconds), (5) exponential backoff on lock contention / DB overload signals, (6) circuit-breaker that aborts run if error rate exceeds threshold (e.g., 5% batch failures) or p95 delete query latency exceeds threshold. Concurrency: enforce single active worker per region via advisory lock/leader election. All limits should be config-driven and have safe defaults.
idempotency_and_correctness: Worker must be safe to rerun without double-counting or deleting in-scope data. Deletes are naturally idempotent with the predicate. The "runs" record stores requested cutoff, effective cutoff applied, and counts; it should tolerate partial progress and mark status as success/partial/failure with an error summary. Add deterministic tests for cutoff computation boundaries (inclusive/exclusive) to avoid off-by-one day issues (especially around UTC day boundaries). Ensure enforcement respects legal_hold and exception flags (ENG-2934) and does not delete records created after cutoff even if partitions are misaligned.
observability_requirements: Metrics (by tenant_id where cardinality is safe; otherwise sampled/aggregated): retention_enforcement_run_total{status, dataset=audit_logs}, retention_enforcement_deleted_rows_total{dataset=audit_logs}, retention_enforcement_delete_latency_ms (histogram), retention_enforcement_lag_seconds (cutoff_now_minus_oldest_remaining), retention_enforcement_batch_errors_total, retention_enforcement_backoff_total, retention_enforcement_skipped_due_to_hold_total. Logs: structured JSON with run_id, tenant_id, dataset, cutoff_ts, batch_size, deleted_rows, duration_ms, error_code. Tracing: optional span around each batch. Dashboards/alerts are tracked in ENG-2944 but this ticket must emit the underlying metrics in a stable form.
acceptance_criteria: Enforcement worker runs on schedule and can be triggered manually (with RBAC/ops safeguards) in non-prod and prod.
Deletes audit log records strictly older than the tenant’s effective retention cutoff, and never deletes records on legal hold / exception hold.
Idempotent retries: rerunning the worker after a partial failure does not delete out-of-scope data and converges to the desired retention state.
Safety limits are enforced (row caps, runtime cap, DB timeout, backoff/circuit-breaker) and are configurable.
Run records are persisted with run_id, dataset, tenant_id (or aggregated), cutoff, start/end timestamps, counts, and status (success/partial/failure).
Metrics and logs are emitted and support an SRE dashboard for lag, delete throughput, and error rate.
Unit/integration tests cover: cutoff boundary, holds respected, batching behavior, failure + retry, and determinism of run record writes.
testing_plan: 1) Unit tests: delete predicate construction; cutoff boundary conditions; hold flags; batch pagination logic; config validation for safety limits. 2) Integration tests (staging DB): seed data across multiple tenants/days, apply different retention policies, run worker, verify remaining rows match expected; simulate transient DB failures and validate retry behavior and run status. 3) Load safety test: run with artificially high deletion volume to validate caps/backoff and ensure DB CPU/locks remain within acceptable thresholds.
rollout_plan: Ship behind feature flag: retention_enforcement_audit_logs. Enable in staging for 48h and verify metrics + no elevated DB load. Canary in prod: internal tenants only, then 3-5 low-volume hosted tenants. Monitor delete latency, lock contention, and retention_lag_seconds. Expand to all hosted tenants, then dedicated tenants. Private deployments: include the worker in the package but default disabled; enable case-by-case with guidance and sizing notes.
open_questions: Do we want to surface per-tenant enforcement status in Console v1 or only aggregated status? (Console surfaces tracked in ENG-2926/ENG-18544). Also, confirm whether we must produce a customer-exportable attestation of run history vs keeping it internal and exposing only last-run status + policy summary.
comments: 2025-01-16 (Ethan Park): Created. This is the enforcement leg for audit log retention; needs to be audit-friendly and safe-by-default. Please align with ADR (hybrid) and keep per-tenant customization in mind.

2025-01-20 (Kevin Osei): Drafted worker design: hourly cron + manual trigger, per-tenant loop, delete in batches with max_rows + max_runtime. Planning to store run records in control-plane DB for evidence and debugging. Will block on ENG-2934 fields for legal hold semantics.

2025-01-22 (Sean Gallagher): Please include hard caps and a circuit-breaker. We’ve had incidents where large deletes saturated DB. Also add an advisory lock so we never run two enforcers at once per region.

2025-01-24 (Marcus Lin): Ensure the enforcement job itself emits an audit event when retention policies are enforced (who triggered manual run; schedule runs can be marked system). We need this for SOC2 evidence and for incident forensics.

2025-01-28 (Jordan Lee): Effective policy evaluation returns an exact cutoff timestamp. Make sure we treat cutoff as exclusive (< cutoff) consistently across datasets. Add golden tests to prevent regressions.

2025-02-03 (Kevin Osei): Implemented in PR #18491. Includes: advisory lock, batch deletes with caps, dry-run, run records, and Prometheus metrics. Remaining: tighten error classification and add one integration test for holds once ENG-2934 lands.

2025-02-06 (Allison Grant): Metrics naming looks good. Please add an alertable lag metric (seconds) and avoid high-cardinality tenant labels in prod by default—use sampling or only emit per-tenant at debug level.

2025-02-10 (Kevin Osei): PR merged. Follow-up: adjust metrics cardinality (default aggregate + allow per-tenant in staging) and add runbook link in service README. Marking ticket Done; monitoring dashboards tracked in ENG-2944.
